cf.title: reindexdb: Fix schema name lookup in parallel mode

input.subject: [PATCH] reindexdb: Fix schema name lookup in parallel mode

verdict_reasoning: No surviving objection questions the fix on master: it is a small client-side bug fix that copies the regnamespace lookup vacuumdb already uses. The one surviving objection, maintenance-fit-1, concerns the request to backpatch through 15. Today `-j -S Sales` reindexes a schema created as "Sales"; after the patch that job fails. Only a committer can decide whether a minor release may do that.

brief.title: reindexdb: fix --schema name lookup in parallel mode
brief.problem: With -j, reindexdb compares --schema arguments directly with pg_namespace.nspname, while serial mode sends REINDEX SCHEMA. So in parallel mode unquoted names are not case folded, quoted names do not match, and a missing schema is silently ignored with exit code 0. Users running reindexdb -S with -j get a run that reindexes nothing and reports success.
brief.proposed_design: Parallel mode resolves each schema argument through a ::regnamespace cast and filters the table list by namespace OID, as vacuumdb does. A missing schema now fails the catalog query before any REINDEX runs, and existing empty schemas still succeed. The patch extends the TAP tests for case folding, a quoted mixed-case name, and a missing schema given with an empty one.
user_visible_surface: reindexdb -S/--schema with -j: arguments now follow identifier rules (case folding, double quotes).
reindexdb -S with -j: a missing schema is now an error with a non-zero exit code.
reindexdb -S with -j: numeric arguments are taken as schema OIDs, and '-' matches nothing.
The error output for a missing schema includes the catalog query text, as -t does today.
author_claims: Parallel mode now matches serial mode for case folding, quoted names and missing schemas.
The approach matches vacuumdb, which uses regnamespace in both serial and parallel modes.
The bug exists since -j was added in Postgres 13, and the author asks to backpatch through 15.
brief.thread_state: Takeshi Ideriha and Joao Rito support the regnamespace approach, and Rito tested v1 and v2 and calls v2 ready for committer. No committer has replied, and the backpatch question is open; v2 does not apply to 15 to 17.
unclear: No committer has said whether the behaviour change is acceptable in back branches, where scripts that passed silently will start to fail.
No backpatch versions for 15 to 17 are posted or tested.
Nobody decided whether parallel mode should differ from REINDEX SCHEMA syntax (U& identifiers, SQL comments, numeric OIDs).
The thread does not say whether the change needs a release note or a documentation update for reindexdb.

objections.title: Backpatching turns silent successes into failures in minor releases
objections.failure_scenario: A site runs a nightly `reindexdb -j 4 -S Sales` job on 16.x, where `Sales` is a schema created as `"Sales"`. After a routine minor update the job exits non-zero and its scheduler raises an alert. Nobody changed the job, and the release notes are the only place the cause is explained.
objections.argument: The fix itself is small and copies the vacuumdb approach, so on master the cost is low. The open part is message #5's request to backpatch through 15, which changes exit codes for scripts that work today, even if they reindex nothing. Message #4 agrees these scripts will now fail and asks for a release note. Message #6 says no port to 15-17 is posted or tested, so the backpatch is not yet ready for review.
objections.author_must_show: Would a master-only fix, or a backpatch that only warns about unmatched schemas, be enough, and if not, why must back branches start failing these scripts?

critic.reasoning: Parallel mode compares the argument with nspname today, so `-S Sales` matches schema "Sales" and reindexes it; after the patch that job fails. No committer has answered the backpatch question, and no port to 15-17 is posted.

refuted.title: Backpatching turns silent successes into failures in minor releases
refuted.failure_scenario: A nightly cron job on 16.x runs `reindexdb -S Sales -j 4` against schema `sales`, or names a schema that was dropped long ago. It has exited 0 for years. After a minor update it exits non-zero every night, and the operator first learns of it from a failed job alert, with no release-note warning.
refuted.argument: Message #5 asks to backpatch through 15. Message #4 calls the new failure a release-note item, and the brief lists this risk as unanswered. Minor releases are expected not to change exit codes for commands that worked before, even when the old result was wrong. Message #6 says v2 does not apply to 15-17 and no port is posted, so a committer cannot yet check the back-branch result.
refuted.author_must_show: Why should 15-18 users get the new missing-schema error in a minor release rather than in the next major release, and what would the release note tell them?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of maintenance-fit-1. Its first example also does not fail: after the patch `-S Sales` folds to `sales`, which exists, so the job starts to reindex and still exits 0.

touch_points.label: SQL-standard conflict or non-standard syntax
touch_points.reason: The regnamespace input accepts numeric OIDs and '-' and does not recognize U& identifiers or SQL comments, unlike REINDEX SCHEMA.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The author asks to backpatch through 15, which changes exit codes for existing `reindexdb -S ... -j` scripts; v2 does not apply to 15 to 17.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: A backpatch needs separate, tested patch versions for 15 to 17, which are not posted.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Why must branches 15 to 18 start failing scripts that pass today, and would a master-only fix or a back-branch warning for unmatched schemas be enough?
Can you post and test patch versions that apply to 15, 16 and 17, since v2 does not apply there?
What would the release note say to users whose `-j -S` job matched a mixed-case schema without double quotes and will now fail?
Does the reindexdb documentation need a change to say that -S arguments follow identifier rules and accept numeric OIDs in parallel mode?
Is it acceptable that serial mode keeps REINDEX SCHEMA syntax while parallel mode uses regnamespace syntax, or should both modes use regnamespace as vacuumdb does?

committability.owner_note: A committer who knows the src/bin/scripts client tools and the back-branch policy for behaviour changes would have to own it; none has replied in the visible thread.
committability.liability: On master, a small client-side change with TAP tests. With a backpatch, the owner also signs for exit-code changes in minor releases of 15 to 18 and for any reports from broken scheduled jobs.
committability.author_follow_up: The author replied to review in message #3 and posted v2 with message #5, which suggests continued engagement.

priority.reason: The patch touches reindexdb.c and one TAP test file, is about 3.5 KB, and reuses the vacuumdb approach. It affects only users of -S with -j, and the remaining decision is the backpatch scope.

provisional_note: The code was not read. Not checked: whether the catalog query quotes the argument safely and is schema-qualified, and how the error for a missing schema reads.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add CREATE SCHEMA ... LIKE support
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds `CREATE SCHEMA <name> LIKE <source_schema>` with `INCLUDING | EXCLUDING` options, which copies the objects of a source schema into a new schema. The first version covered tables and indexes; later versions added foreign keys and partitions, with warnings when an object references another schema.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Álvaro Herrera questioned adding DDL syntax for this at all, given the many hard cases and the extra clauses proposed for CREATE SCHEMA. He suggested building on the DDL-generating functions proposed in other threads. The author agreed that a function such as pg_get_schema_ddl() seemed a better way. The visible messages do not show a later version or an explicit closing decision.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This whole thing seems like a giant can of worms, and I'm not sure it's
a good idea to add DDL syntax for it.

precedents_retrieved.title: Tab completion for CREATE SCHEMA AUTHORIZATION
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds psql tab completion for create schema authorization and for the words after create schema <name>. Later versions also complete CURRENT_ROLE, CURRENT_USER and SESSION_USER for other commands that take a role, and merge the duplicated role list queries.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author did not post a new version after review comments in August 2021, so Michael Paquier marked the entry returned with feedback in December. The open comments asked for comments on each role list query and for completion after create schema authorization <role>. Reviewers also pointed out that the patch offered SESSION_USER for create user mapping, where the syntax does not list it, and left out USER.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This patch has been waiting on author for more than a couple of weeks,
so I have marked it as returned with feedback in the CF app.

precedents_retrieved.title: Prevent extension creation in temporary schemas
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch first made create extension fail when the target schema is a temporary schema, as alter extension set schema already does. After objections, the author dropped that and changed psql's \dx and \dx+ to hide extensions in other sessions' temporary schemas.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Chris Travers objected that other objects such as types can already be created in temporary schemas, so blocking extensions only would add another special case. The author dropped the block and kept only the \dx and \dx+ fix, which Chris Travers marked Ready for Committer. The author then found that a second session cannot create an extension already created in another session's temporary schema, but \dx no longer lists it. He returned the patch because it does not solve the root problem and makes things more confusing.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
The patch as it stands does not actually solve the root problem and
makes things a bit confusing, so I am marking it as returned with
feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: psql: add schema size information to \dn+
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a Size column to psql's \dn+ output that shows the total on-disk size of the tables, materialized views and sequences in each schema. psql computes the size client-side with pg_total_relation_size(), for servers 8.1 and later.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Robert Haas noted that computing the size can take a long time on a big or busy database. Tom Lane asked whether \dn+ could fail or give misleading answers for users without permissions on some tables, and said the feature would block future tightening of access to size information. Julien Rouhaud noted that pg_total_relation_size() does no permission check at all. The author withdrew the patch and offered a server-side pg_schema_size() function as a possible alternative.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Also, even if
we allow people to get size info on tables they can't read today,
having this feature would be a roadblock to tightening that in
the future.

precedents_retrieved.title: Various small unrelated doc patches: plpgsql, schemas, permissions, oidvector
precedents_retrieved.summary: Karl Pinc proposed a set of small, mostly unrelated documentation changes to plpgsql, schemas, permissions and the oidvector type, later split into a numbered patch series. Some patches changed one line, while others added short overview sections, for example on role management and on search_path for routines.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers asked for changes: David G. Johnston proposed rewrites or a different approach for several patches (0009 to 0012, 0015), and Shubham Khanna listed spelling errors. In December 2023 the author said he could not send new patches for two weeks, and in March 2024 he said he still had not done the rework. No updated patch appears in the visible messages before the entry was returned with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_get_constraintdef: Schema qualify foreign tables unless pretty printing is enabled
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes pg_get_constraintdef schema-qualify the referenced table in a foreign key's REFERENCES clause when pretty printing is off, as pg_get_indexdef already does. The goal is constraint definitions that can be recreated on another system with a different search_path.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane said pg_get_indexdef is the odd one out, since most generate_relation_name calls in ruleutils.c ignore the pretty flag, and Alvaro Herrera judged the patch too small for making PRETTYFLAG_SCHEMA work consistently. Tom asked for a clearly defined rule on which call sites qualify names, with a documented helper function. The author did not reply to these reviews, and Michael Paquier returned the patch after six weeks without a reply.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: In other words, I think your patch is too small.

precedents_retrieved.title: ALTER TABLE SET LOGGED/UNLOGGED on a partitioned table does nothing silently
precedents_retrieved.summary: Make ALTER TABLE SET LOGGED/UNLOGGED on a partitioned table propagate to its partitions instead of completing silently without changing anything. The discussion widened to how ALTER TABLE/INDEX actions in general should behave on partitioned tables, including whether future partitions should inherit the parent's setting.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew the entry. Review showed that the fix depended on agreeing a general policy for how many ALTER TABLE/INDEX actions should recurse to partitions and apply to future partitions, and the author said he could not take the time to research and fix those other issues. A stopgap patch from Bharath Rupireddy that emitted a warning and added a documentation note was posted, but the entry was withdrawn instead.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: However, I think I'll withdraw this CF entry since I'm not sure I can take time for the time being to research and fix other various ALTER TABLE/INDEX issues.

precedents_retrieved.title: Connection string usage for Core Postgresql client applications
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch documents that the dbname argument or option of several client applications (clusterdb, pgbench, pg_dump, pg_restore, reindexdb, vacuumdb) accepts a connection string. The author also suggested making all client applications accept connection strings with the same syntax, such as a common -d switch.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew the patch after review. Laurenz Albe supported it and asked for wording changes and for createdb and dropdb to be covered. The author replied that she was not satisfied with a documentation-only patch and wanted every client application to accept the same syntax, so she would rethink the approach.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I'm not very satisfied with this patch. I think I want to go further with unifying connection string usage.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found. The only listed row, [P5], reverts a change that forbade DROP SCHEMA on temporary namespaces. It shares only the word "schema", and its recorded reason has nothing to do with reindexdb or with how client tools look up names. No thread message points to an earlier discussion of this idea. The open backpatch question belongs to another angle.

The standards-compat case against the fix on master is weak. It reuses vacuumdb's regnamespace scheme and -t's regclass lookup. The thread already settled that OIDs and '-' are accepted (messages #2-#4), so I dropped that point.

The patch changes only how the reindexdb client builds its catalog query for -S with -j. It adds no on-disk format, WAL record, catalog column, wire protocol message or extension ABI, so this angle has nothing to object to. The back-branch behaviour change is for another angle.

No new privileges or exposure. The cast resolves names only for the connected user, so schema existence stays as visible as pg_namespace already makes it. Message #4 shows the argument is quoted as a string literal before the regnamespace cast, the same scheme as vacuumdb and -t. A code check could still confirm the catalog query is schema-qualified under the scripts' secure search_path.

For master, I see no maintenance or fit objection. The change is a small client-side fix that reuses the regnamespace and regclass lookups already in vacuumdb and in reindexdb -t. It adds no hot-path cost and no new API.

This is a bug fix in reindexdb parallel mode. It reuses the regnamespace lookup that vacuumdb and reindexdb -t already use, so it adds no new mechanism. No existing feature or extension removes the bug, and the serial-mode workaround gives up -j. [P5] is a revert about DROP SCHEMA on temp namespaces, which is unrelated.

This is a bug fix: with -j, reindexdb -S silently reindexes nothing and exits 0, which messages #1 and #4 reproduce. Anyone who uses -S with -j benefits, and users who do not use them bear no cost. Demand does not need separate proof for a fix to silent wrong behaviour that brings parallel mode in line with serial mode and vacuumdb. The back-branch behaviour change is a different angle. [P5] is not relevant.
